The Bachelors (German: Der Hagestolz, lit. 'The Bachelor'), also published as The Recluse, is a novel by the Austrian writer Adalbert Stifter. It was published as a novella in the anthology series Iris in 1844 and as a full-length novel in 1850.. The young man Victor is an orphan and has promised himself to never get married. He visits his only known relative, a reclusive and misanthropic uncle who lives alone in a decaying mansion on an island.
